sections.h2: Selling an Owatonna house without a long wait
sections.html:
The quickest exit is usually a cash buyer who takes the place exactly as you leave it. Hiring an agent or selling on your own takes longer, because both lean on open houses and on the buyer's lender signing off.

As the Steele County seat, Owatonna has the recorder, the treasurer and the county finance office all in town. A closing stays simple provided the house has no rental license problems, no delinquent taxes and a clear answer about flooding.

Owners occupy three of every four Owatonna homes. The city sits on both sides of the Straight River, with the oldest neighborhoods on low ground along its eastern side and newer homes along the Maple Creek ravine. Seven public school buildings were repaired or replaced under bonds voters approved in 2015 and 2019, and the new Owatonna High School opened to students on September 5, 2023.

There are 11,018 households here, averaging 2.36 people, and most residents (88.3 percent) were in the same house a year earlier.

Record rain from September 22 to 24, 2010 sent the Straight River and Maple Creek over their banks, and developments built in the floodplains of both streams were completely inundated. Not sure if your parcel lies in a floodplain? The county or the city can tell you.

If your property sits near the river or the creek, write down any water in the basement, drainage fixes or insurance claims you know about before you list. Minnesota law makes you disclose material facts you know about in writing, and earlier flooding is the kind of thing buyers ask about. Keep receipts for sump pumps, regrading or waterproofing, because they help show that a problem was handled. A cash buyer will usually ask the same questions, so an honest written answer up front saves time and avoids a price change late in the process. If you have never had water in the house, say so plainly in the disclosure.

Chapter 115 of the city code makes the Fire Department the office where every rental is registered and given a city license. An inspection is scheduled, and the license is issued once the property passes and the fees are paid. A license is valid for two years.

  • Use one application per rental address.
  • File a fresh application the first time a property is rented, once a license runs out, and whenever ownership changes.
  • Renting without a valid license is a misdemeanor, and every day of renting counts as a separate violation.

If your Owatonna house is rented, make sure the license is current before the closing date. A buyer who intends to keep tenants must apply for a new license after the sale. The Fire Department's number is 507-444-2454.

sections.h2: Steele County Recorder fees and the deed tax
sections.html:
The Steele County Recorder charges $46 to record a document and $54 for a well disclosure statement. Mailed or dropped-off documents are turned around in 10 business days or less, and appointments are available during business hours. Splitting a tax parcel costs $100, paid to the county treasurer.

Minnesota sets the deed tax in Minnesota Statutes section 287.21. The rate is 0.33 percent of net consideration above $3,000, collected by the county as the deed is recorded. A transfer with no consideration, or $3,000 or less, pays a flat $1.65.

Before closing, request an itemized settlement statement from the title company that shows the fee, the tax and any unpaid property tax.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates and payment options
sections.html:
Steele County mails real estate tax statements each March, and every owner receives one even if a lender pays the bill. Real estate tax comes due in two installments, May 15 and October 15. If a date lands on a weekend, the deadline moves to the next business day. Agricultural second-half taxes come due in mid-November, and taxes left unpaid at year end become delinquent on January 1.

You can pay at the Finance office inside the County Administration Building, 630 Florence Avenue, send a check to Steele County Finance, P.O. Box 890, or leave it in the drop box out front. The drop box is cleared at 8 a.m. the next business day, and later deposits must include a penalty.

  • A card payment adds 2.5 percent, minimum $1.50.
  • A Visa debit card adds $3.95.
  • E-checks under $10,000 add $1.50.
  • Direct debit carries no fee.

To use direct debit, get the authorization form to the Finance office by April 30 for the first half or by September 30 for the second.

sections.h2: Order of work for a fast Owatonna closing
sections.html: Begin before you accept anything. Look up your property tax status, because any unpaid balance is taken from your proceeds. For a rental, call the Fire Department about the license. Note any basement water you have seen, and collect receipts for pumps or drainage work. Once an offer comes in, have the closing date, the check amount and the party responsible for each fee put in writing. Next the title company drafts the deed and the settlement statement, and you should expect them to ask for your tax statement and any rental license papers. The Recorder charges $46 to record the deed and $54 for the well disclosure, and the county collects the deed tax at recording. Read the itemized settlement statement before signing and compare each line with the written offer.

sections.h2: What to ask an Owatonna cash buyer
sections.html:
Ask for the offer on paper and read every line.

  • Which party orders the title work and pays for recording?
  • How will the buyer handle past flood or drainage issues in the disclosure?
  • If a rental license is active, who finishes the term?
  • What is the exact payout after deed tax and any county balance?

Also ask whether the buyer will let you stay a few days after closing to finish moving. A direct offer lets you set the move date, and that is its main benefit over a listing. Weigh that against what an open-market sale would leave once repairs and months of upkeep are paid.

faqs.q: Can I hand my Owatonna rental license to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. Ownership changes require a new application, so the buyer applies in their own name. The city issues two-year licenses once an inspection is passed and fees are paid.

faqs.q: What deed tax applies to an Owatonna sale?
faqs.a: The tax equals 0.33 percent of the price once the price passes $3,000, and a sale at or under that amount pays a flat $1.65. The county collects it at the recording stage.

faqs.q: Where can I pay Steele County property tax face to face?
faqs.a: Visit the Finance office on the ground level of the County Administration Building, 630 Florence Avenue, on a weekday. A drop box stands out front by the flagpoles.

faqs.q: What does a well disclosure cost in Steele County?
faqs.a: The recording office charges $54 for a well disclosure statement or certificate. The $46 deed recording fee is separate.

faqs.q: Should I mention the 2010 flood when selling an Owatonna house?
faqs.a: Yes, if your property is near the Straight River or Maple Creek and you know of water damage, mention it. The disclosure covers material facts you know of, and a buyer will look for flood history in that area.
